questions.stem: What force keeps a satellite in orbit around the Earth?

options.text: The thrust from the satellite's engines
Magnetic force
Air resistance
Gravitational force, acting as the centripetal force

questions.explanation: Gravitational attraction between the satellite and Earth provides the centripetal force needed to keep the satellite on a curved orbital path. The force acts towards the centre of the Earth.

questions.stem: What are the characteristics of a geostationary orbit?

options.text: It is above the equator at 35,786 km altitude with a period of exactly 24 hours
It is at 400 km altitude and is used for the International Space Station
It is at any altitude and has any period
It passes over the poles and has a period of 90 minutes

questions.explanation: A geostationary orbit is above the equator at 35,786 km altitude with an orbital period of exactly 24 hours. Because it matches Earth's rotation, the satellite appears stationary from the ground, making it ideal for communications and broadcasting.

questions.stem: Why do satellites in lower orbits travel faster than those in higher orbits?

options.text: Because they have more powerful engines
Because there is less air resistance at lower altitudes
Because the gravitational field is stronger at lower altitudes, requiring a higher speed for a stable orbit
Because they are lighter

questions.explanation: At lower altitudes, the gravitational field is stronger, providing greater centripetal acceleration. For the satellite to maintain a stable circular orbit at this smaller radius, it must travel faster. From v = sqrt(GM/r), a smaller r gives a larger v.

questions.stem: What does Kepler's Third Law state about orbital motion?

options.text: All orbits are perfectly circular
Heavier satellites orbit faster
Satellites always travel at the same speed
The orbital period squared is proportional to the orbital radius cubed

questions.explanation: Kepler's Third Law states that T squared is proportional to r cubed. This means that satellites further from the central body have longer orbital periods. For example, the Moon (384,000 km) takes 27.3 days, while the ISS (400 km altitude) takes only 92 minutes.

questions.stem: Why do astronauts on the International Space Station appear weightless?

options.text: Because the ISS shields them from gravity
Because they and the station are in free fall together, falling at the same rate around the Earth
Because the ISS has artificial gravity generators
Because there is no gravity at 400 km altitude

questions.explanation: At 400 km altitude, gravity is still about 90% of its surface value. Astronauts appear weightless because they and the ISS are in free fall together, both falling towards Earth at the same rate. There is no contact force between them, creating the sensation of weightlessness.

questions.stem: Which type of orbit is used by GPS navigation satellites?

options.text: Polar orbit
Low Earth orbit at 400 km
Medium Earth orbit at about 20,200 km
Geostationary orbit at 35,786 km

questions.explanation: GPS satellites orbit in medium Earth orbit (MEO) at an altitude of about 20,200 km with an orbital period of approximately 12 hours. A constellation of these satellites provides global positioning coverage.

The speed at which a satellite orbits the Earth
The speed at which the Earth rotates
The minimum speed needed to escape a planet's gravitational field without further propulsion

questions.explanation: Escape velocity is the minimum speed an object needs to leave a planet's gravitational field without any further propulsion. For Earth, this is 11.2 km/s. It depends on the mass and radius of the body being escaped from.
